key_insight: Proximity to a metal-insulator transition can be used to tune correlated-oxide transparent conductors so they gain a wider optical window while retaining useful near-Fermi-level states.
engineering_relevance: This provides a practical materials-design rule for optimizing transparent electrodes for silicon photovoltaics and other optoelectronic devices by balancing transparency against conductivity.
method: Used epitaxial Ti-substituted SrVO3 films as a tunable model system.
Varied composition to approach the metal-insulator transition and simultaneously track optical and transport properties.
Analyzed performance with a Haacke figure of merit to identify the best composition range.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports a systematic broadening of the optical window toward silicon-relevant wavelengths, with the best figure-of-merit occurring near the composition-driven metal-insulator transition.
watch_item: Near the optimal transparency range, carrier depletion and disorder reduce coherent transport, so the approach may be limited by the loss of metallic conductivity and sensitivity to disorder.
paper_title: Engineering Correlated Transparent Conductors via Metal-Insulator Transition Proximity
